title: Development and Internal Validation of a Mortality Risk Score in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease Receiving Dual Antiplatelet Therapy after Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
content: Background: Patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) who receive dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain exposed to residual ischemic and mortality risk. High on-treatment platelet reactivity has been associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, yet platelet function testing is not always available for routine triage. Aim: This study aimed to develop an interpretable clinical score based on routinely available variables to identify CAD patients on DAPT who have an increased risk of mortality and may require closer assessment of residual platelet reactivity. Methods: We analyzed a retrospective cohort of 1,600 adults with CAD admitted between 2022 and 2024. Twenty demographic, clinical, laboratory, and instrumental variables were evaluated. The dataset was randomly divided into training and validation subsets in a 3:1 ratio. Predictors were selected using univariable and multivariable logistic regression with stepwise selection. Continuous variables were categorized using Weight of Evidence binning, and a point-based score was derived from the final regression model. Model performance was assessed using ROC analysis, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Results: The final score included age ≥57 years, estimated glomerular filtration rate <45 mL/min/1.73 m², body mass index ≥25 kg/m², troponin I ≥100, prior myocardial infarction, and current smoking. Each additional point increased the odds of mortality by 39% (OR 1.39; 95% CI 1.29-1.51; p < 0.001). In the training cohort, the AUC was 0.654. A Youden-index threshold of approximately 6 points improved sensitivity to 0.41, with specificity of 0.80 and accuracy of 0.72. In the validation subset, sensitivity was 0.53, specificity was 0.70, accuracy was 0.70, and AUC was 0.61. Conclusions: A simple mortality risk score based on routinely available clinical variables demonstrated modest but clinically interpretable discrimination in CAD patients receiving DAPT. The score may help identify patients who require closer follow-up and consideration of platelet reactivity assessment. Prospective multicenter validation and direct incorporation of platelet function testing are required before routine clinical implementation.
